summary:
Our project is a space exploration survival game in which players travel across the universe, discover and collect resources, construct structures, and manage their vital needs while facing the challenges of environments far beyond Earth.

The game's main objective is to spark curiosity and enthusiasm for space exploration by offering an engaging, interactive experience that introduces players to the challenges of living and surviving beyond our planet.

Despite rapid technological advancements and growing ambitions in the space sector, public interest in space exploration has been declining, contributing to a shortage of skilled professionals. Reversing this trend is essential to inspiring the next generation of talent and meeting the industry's growing demand for qualified specialists.

Our project aims to help address this challenge by making space exploration more accessible, engaging, and inspiring.
details:
Moon Base 101 is an educational space survival game that puts players in charge of an expedition across the Moon, Mars, and Venus. Players gather resources, build and power a base, and manage oxygen, food, water, temperature, and suit integrity. To complete the main mission, they survey four sites on each world, return to the Moon, and transmit their findings to Earth.

The game teaches mission planning through decisions with consequences. During a solar storm, for example, players must decide whether to finish a survey or seek shelter. A base also needs working systems for power, oxygen, and supplies, so building one is only the first step. Survey sites explain what was measured and why it matters. Our goal is to help younger players understand how an expedition’s resources, equipment, and environment affect one another. The simulation simplifies real spaceflight so those relationships are easy to see and learn from.

We built the desktop game in Rust using the Bevy game engine and wgpu for rendering. The mobile browser client uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Canvas. In local multiplayer, one computer runs the shared simulation. Desktop players connect over TCP, while phone players join through a browser using WebSocket. We packaged the game for Windows and for Linux with X11/Vulkan or Wayland/OpenGL. English and Polish use shared JSON translation files.

Our team considered how much detail a first-time player could absorb, how to make each world feel distinct, and how friends could play together on different devices. We used visible objectives, short prompts, and explanations at survey sites to make the campaign approachable. Sandbox mode lets players experiment with base building and exploration at their own pace. In co-op, players can divide the work—for example, one can maintain the base while another drives a rover to a research site.
